column2: The 3 Million Technical Talent programme, Africa's largest state-backed tech-skills drive, training young people in coding, data, AI, cloud and cybersecurity across all 36 states and the FCT.
column3: It prepares young Nigerians for jobs they can do from anywhere in the world.

column1: How many young people have enrolled in 3MTT?
column2: Over 270,000 learners have enrolled, after a first phase that trained 30,000 fellows with 100+ training providers.
column3: Hundreds of thousands of young people gaining skills for the digital economy.

column1: How big is the iDICE fund for start-ups and creatives?
column2: Over $600 million, co-financed by the African Development Bank, Islamic Development Bank and France's AFD, supporting tech start-ups and creative hubs.
column3: Funding for young entrepreneurs, musicians, film-makers and developers.

column1: How many Nigerians now have a National Identification Number?
column2: Over 100 million verified NIN records, with self-service updates and contactless enrolment via phone.
column3: One ID that links your bank, passport, SIM and benefits, and helps fight fraud.

column1: What protection did telecom masts and fibre cables get?
column2: They were classified as Critical National Infrastructure, making vandalism and illegal shutdowns a serious offence.
column3: Fewer network outages from vandalised masts and cut cables.

column2: A plan to connect all 774 local government secretariats to high-speed internet by fibre and satellite.
column3: Digital government services closer to every community.

column1: What did NITDA build for Nigerian languages?
column2: Nigeria's own multilingual AI language model, built to work in Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo.
column3: AI that speaks our languages, not just English.

column2: A free-to-air digital TV service launched on 17 June 2026, with 100+ channels and no monthly subscription.
column3: Families can watch TV without paying monthly fees.

column1: What Made-in-Nigeria products has NASENI produced?
column2: More than 44 commercial products, including Nigerian-made laptops, phones and electric tricycles; a solar park in Gora, Nasarawa is due in 2026.
column3: Building things at home creates jobs and saves foreign exchange.
